title: Parental Absence and Agency: The Household Characteristics of Hazardous Forms of Child Labour in Nepal
abstract: This study examines how household circumstances and children’s agency relate to hazardous forms of child labour in Nepal. Using nationally representative household evidence, it investigates the roles of parental absence and household vulnerability in children’s exposure to dangerous work. The analysis emphasizes that children’s work decisions occur within family conditions and constraints, so policies addressing hazardous labour need to consider household structure and the support available to children.
